evidence.excerpt: In garment production, adjacent cutting plans laid on the same spreading table ideally consume pieces from the same fabric roll to reduce changeover time and shade variation. This paper formulates roll-to-plan assignment and plan sequencing as a combined optimisation problem and solves it with a beam search procedure guided by a composite objective weighting material utilisation (70%) and roll changeover frequency (30%). The beam width is varied from 5 to 50 and evaluated on planning instances with 15 to 60 cutting plans drawn from production records of two Serbian garment manufacturers. At beam width 20, the procedure reduces average changeover frequency by 27% relative to first-fit sequencing while reducing material utilisation by only 0.4 percentage points. Solution time is under 4 seconds for all instances. The paper also reports a sensitivity analysis showing that the 70/30 objective weighting is robust within the range 60/40 to 80/20 for the tested instances.
